newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 96-97 sugar consumption seen down - Sparks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 96-97 sugar consumption seen down - Sparks.

text.p: Sparks Companies Inc forecast that Mexico's 1996-1997 crop year consumption of sugar will drop around six percent to 4.1 million tonnes raw vale, Sparks' senior analyst for tropical commodiites said here Thursday.

"While strong growth in sugar consumption was experienced in the early 1990s, consumption the last two years has trended downward," Peter Buzzanell told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference.
Sparks put Mexico consumption at 4.31 million tonnes in 1994-1995, a 24 percent increase over the mid-1980s figure of 3.47 million tonnes.

"With sugar production forecast at 4.6 million tonnes and consumption at 4.1 million, the implied 1996-1997 surplus of 500,000 tonnes is larger than last season's level of nearly 300,000 tonnes. This situation is forcing the Mexican sugar industry into policy decisions that aim to reduce price- depressing stocks in the country," Buzzanell said.
Mexican sugar industrialists have a long standing pact with the government to hold strategic stocks in the country to guarantee national supplies.
